# v2.99

This stable release rolls up dev pre-releases **v2.97-dev, v2.98-dev and
v2.99-dev**. It is a security and hardening release: **updating promptly is
recommended.**

Most of it concerns how quickly a permission change takes effect, who can see
what, and what leaves the system in an exported file. Nothing changes in how the
application is set up or operated, and no action is needed on upgrade.

## Fixed

- **Changing someone's role now applies immediately, instead of whenever they
  next sign in.** A person's role used to travel with their signed-in session,
  so changing it while they were logged in left the old role in force for as
  long as that session lasted — up to eight hours. Someone you had just moved
  out of an administrator role could keep using administrator pages, and keep
  the company access that went with it, for the rest of the working day. The
  Users page showed the new role the whole time, which made it look as though
  the change had taken.

  Changing a role now ends that person's open sessions. They sign back in and
  continue with their new role, and the change applies from their very next
  action.

- **"Require MFA at next login" now takes effect on the current session too.**
  Ticking it for someone already signed in previously did nothing until they
  happened to log out, which could be days. They are now asked to set up
  two-factor authentication straight away.

  Editing only a display name does not sign anyone out, and changing your own
  role keeps you signed in — you carry on immediately with the new role rather
  than being logged out by your own edit.

- **"Last imported" timestamps are now limited to the companies you can see.**
  This one small read was not company-checked, so any signed-in person —
  including a read-only account — could ask whether another company had ever
  had an import, and when. On its own that is a date and a yes/no, but company
  references are sequential, so it also allowed the list of companies to be
  worked out. Asking about a company you have no access to now gives exactly the
  same answer as a company that has never been imported.

- **Exported CSV files can no longer carry a spreadsheet formula.** A
  spreadsheet treats a value starting with certain characters as a formula to
  run rather than text to show, so a name or title that merely passed through
  the system could take effect in the spreadsheet of whoever opened the file.
  Those values are now marked as text. This matters most for **scheduled
  exports**, which write files to a shared drive on a timer with nobody there to
  notice anything unusual before the file is opened.

  Ordinary content is unchanged — including negative numbers and percentages,
  which are still exported exactly as before — and Excel exports were already
  unaffected, so they are untouched.

- **Delivery settings now return only the fields the settings page actually
  uses.** Previously everything stored was returned except a fixed list of
  known-sensitive fields, so anything added later would have been returned by
  default. It now works the other way round: a short list of fields is shown and
  everything else is withheld. Passwords and tokens are still never sent to the
  page — it is only told whether one is set.

- **The version number is no longer published to the sign-in page.** Anyone who
  could reach the login screen could read the exact version without signing in,
  which is useful mainly to somebody matching a system against a list of known
  issues. It is now sent only to people who have signed in. Nothing changes in
  what you see.

- **A training or offering link is checked before it is saved.** These fields
  accept a web address and until now accepted anything at all; they now take
  ordinary `http://` and `https://` addresses only. Saving something else tells
  you why, and a spreadsheet import reports the rows it could not accept and
  carries on with the rest. Anything already saved that is not a web address is
  no longer shown as a clickable link. This one is a precaution rather than a
  repair — testing confirmed such a link already did nothing when clicked — but
  the system no longer depends on the browser for that.

- **Editing a user who no longer exists** now reports that plainly instead of
  failing with a server error.

## Changed

- **Spreadsheet imports check the file before opening it.** Import pages now
  refuse a file over 25&nbsp;MB, an empty file, or one that is not a CSV or
  Excel file, and say so. Previously an oversized or mistyped file was read in
  full first, which could leave the page unresponsive with no explanation. This
  is a limit in the browser only — nothing about what can be imported has
  changed.

## Internal

- The rule that a system-wide administrator also counts as an administrator was
  written out separately in three places. It now has one definition, so the
  parts of the system that enforce it cannot drift apart.

## Upgrading

No action needed, and nothing to reconfigure. The one visible change is that
people whose role you change will be asked to sign in again.
